feature: very thick, deeply fissured blocky grey bark with lichen; large spreading oak crown; lobed bristle-tipped oak leaves on the ground
text_seen: Tape around trunk: hook meets the tape at about 113 in (9 ft 5 in) in one frame and about 119 in in the second frame; circumference about 113 to 119 in, DBH about 36 to 38 in. A small rusted metal tag plate is nailed to the trunk, nothing legible.
match_reason: Large oak in section A; roster 02 Turkey oak pin 20 m away and the Nov 2 photo matched to 02 is 12 m away. Bark is too rugged for northern red oak. No leaf or acorn in hand, so red oak stays an alternative.
maintenance_note: Large burl at the base on the uphill side and a second burl higher on the road side; old pruning stub on the road side; otherwise full crown. Worth an arborist look at the base burls.
notes: IMG_0xxx and IMG_9xxx pairs are the same frames under two file names. Tree stands at the road edge beside a house with a red Japanese maple in its yard.

feature: plaque names the tree; young slender grey-barked tree with the low forking habit of a redbud, leafless on Oct 24
text_seen: Plaque: 'Cercis canadensis / Eastern Redbud/Judas Tree / In honor of / Sue Bush's 10 years of service / to the Hingham Cemetery / Planted 2019'
match_reason: Species matches 31 Eastern redbud, pin 9 m, Nov 2 photo of 31 at 7 m. A second young bare tree stands a few meters behind it in IMG_9245 (right), which is probably 32 Appalachian Red redbud; it has no close frames in this unit.
maintenance_note: Young tree, single leader, no damage seen. Small bark wound at the base of the trunk in IMG_9249 (old, callused).
notes: Unit split: the redbud frames and the linden frames are two different trees.

feature: heart shaped, sharply serrate leaves on basal sprouts; big burly trunk base; same tree as U020 which has leaf close-ups
match_reason: No linden on the roster in section A. Nearest pins are 04 larch (3 m), 31 and 32 redbuds; none agree. Roster 28 Linden is in section D, 130 m away. Propose as new; see U020 for the same tree.
maintenance_note: Large burls around the base, basal sprouting, leaf spot on the sprout leaves. Mature tree beside the road; an arborist should check the base.
notes: U020 (16:15) is the same linden; keep one record.

feature: heart shaped, sharply serrate, asymmetric leaf base; furrowed vertical bark with burls
match_reason: Same linden as the second tree in U017 (7 m apart by GPS, 6 minutes later). No roster linden in section A; 04 larch pin 7 m and 40 white pine 11 m do not agree.
maintenance_note: Burls at the base and up the trunk; leaf spot (dark blotches) on the leaves. Species within Tilia (americana vs cordata vs europaea) needs a flower or fruit check next summer.
notes: Same tree as new-U017; one roster proposal for both units.

feature: tall straight pine with plated bark and a high crown by the stone wall and road; one landscape frame only
match_reason: Taken 15 s before U028 (IMG_2467), which is the trunk base of the same pine; U024's GPS (42.2430) is 60 m off every pin and is probably a fix error, U028's GPS is 11 m from 40 Eastern white pine and 11 m from the Nov 2 photos of both 39 and 40. See U028 for the cone conflict.
notes: Treat U024 and U028 as one tree.

feature: plated scaly bark at the base with small egg shaped cones (about 2 to 3 in) on the ground
match_reason: Position fits 40 Eastern white pine (pin 11 m, Nov 2 photo 11 m). Conflict: the small egg shaped cones on the ground do not fit Pinus strobus (cones 4 to 8 in, slender); they fit Pinus cembra (roster 39, Nov 2 photo also 11 m away) or a red or Austrian pine. The cones may have blown in from another tree. Needs a needle count (5 per bundle = white or Swiss stone pine, 2 = red or Austrian).
notes: One of the five most uncertain units. Same tree as U024.

feature: cone 4.75 in long with wavy, toothed scale tips; pendulous branchlets; short four sided needles on orange brown twigs
text_seen: Tape on cone: about 4.75 in. Tape around trunk at chest height: about 80 in circumference (DBH about 25 in). Tape on twig: needles about 0.5 to 0.8 in. Headstones in frame: KIMBALL, WALLACE, McCARTER.
match_reason: No upright Norway spruce on the roster. Nearest pins 32 and 31 redbuds (22 to 24 m) and 05 red oak (29 m) do not agree. Roster 06 is a weeping Norway spruce 70 m south and is not this tree. Propose as new.
maintenance_note: Tall straight stem, full crown, heavy cone crop, lichen on the lower trunk. The trunk base frames (IMG_9297, 2477 to 2479) show orange grey plates; if those are a neighboring pine rather than this spruce the measurement still belongs to the spruce (IMG_9303).
notes: IMG_2xxx and IMG_9xxx frames repeat the same views. Tree stands on the hill with the chapel behind it.

feature: one landscape frame of a tall bare crowned deciduous tree with furrowed bark beside the spruce, chapel behind
match_reason: Could be 05 Northern red oak (pin 29 m) but nothing in the frame decides it. Not matched.
notes: Second tree in the unit; one frame only.

feature: large broad crowned deciduous tree on the hill among old slate stones; no leaf, bark or fruit frame
text_seen: Headstone: 'In memory of William Hersey' (old slate stone in front of the tree); obelisk at right.
match_reason: Nearest pins 27 Japanese maple (21 m), 40 white pine (30 m) and 01 Bloodgood (31 m) are all wrong for a large deciduous tree. 35 European beech (official map, about 45 m) is the only large deciduous candidate nearby but nothing in the frame confirms it. Not matched.
notes: One of the five most uncertain units. Needs a bark or leaf frame next visit.

feature: short flat two ranked needles with pale undersides on fine drooping twigs, tiny cones under 1 in; feathery drooping crown
match_reason: No hemlock on the roster. Nearest pins 05 red oak and 32 and 31 redbuds (25 to 27 m) do not agree. Propose as new.
maintenance_note: Full crown with some dead inner twigs (normal shading). Check the undersides of twigs for hemlock woolly adelgid (white wool) each spring.
notes: Stands on the hilltop a few meters east of the U031 spruce.

feature: narrow interlacing ridged grey bark and long exposed surface roots over the slope; the same tree is confirmed by leaf and samara in U043 two minutes later
match_reason: 29 Norway maple pin 14 m, Nov 2 photo of 29 at 12 m.
maintenance_note: Extensive exposed surface roots on the downhill side, some scuffed; keep foot traffic and mowers off them.
notes: Single frame repeated under several file names.

feature: narrow interlacing ridged grey bark and long exposed surface roots over the slope; the same tree is confirmed by leaf and samara in U043 two minutes later
match_reason: All three files are the same frame as U040; the U042 GPS (50 m from 29) is a copy or fix error, not a different tree.
maintenance_note: Extensive exposed surface roots on the downhill side, some scuffed; keep foot traffic and mowers off them.
notes: Single frame repeated under several file names.

feature: samaras with wings spread nearly flat (180 degrees); five lobed leaf with long sharp pointed lobes
text_seen: Tape around trunk: overlap at about 80 in circumference (DBH about 25 in).
match_reason: 29 Norway maple pin 7 m, Nov 2 photo of 29 at 5 m, species agrees.
maintenance_note: Full broad crown, no dieback seen. IMG_9339 (last frame, 16:44) shows flaky plated bark with heavy lichen that does not look like this maple; it may be the larch (roster 04, Nov 2 photo 17 m away) or another conifer beside it. Cannot tell from one frame.
notes: UUID named files and IMG_25xx files are the same frames twice.

feature: deciduous conifer with needles in rosettes on spur shoots, turning gold, pendulous twigs loaded with small cones; the plaque on the neighboring young larch names Larix decidua
text_seen: Tape around the mid sized larch: about 39 in circumference (DBH about 12 in). Tape around the big trunk: 60 in at the hook (DBH about 19 in).
match_reason: Roster 04 is the only larch and is listed as 'tamarack or European larch, pending cone check'. Position is loose: the 04 pin is 58 m north and the Nov 2 photo of 04 is about 40 m west; the nearest pin here is 05 red oak (26 m). Species agrees and nothing else on the roster is a larch. Which of the two or three larches in this group is the roster's 04 cannot be told from the photos.
maintenance_note: Heavy lichen on the trunks; the big trunk has deep scaly grey plates. Crowns full. The cone count on the pendulous twigs is very high this year.
notes: A group of larches: the big one (60 in), a mid one (39 in) and the 1999 plaque tree (separate entry). Larch confirmed; the roster's 'pending cone check' can close as Larix decidua if the plaque tree is the same species as its neighbors, which the needles and cones support. Box tomb and the orange house on the road behind.

feature: plaque names the species; needles sprouting from the slim trunk are larch rosettes
text_seen: Plaque: 'Larix decidua / European larch / Gift of / Derby Academy / Class 1999'. Tape around trunk: about 20.5 in circumference (DBH about 6.5 in).
match_reason: Young plaqued larch beside the mature larches. The roster has one larch (04); if 04 is the plaqued tree then this is 04 and the mature ones are new, if 04 is a mature one then this is new. Listed as new with 04 as the alternative so the number is not invented.
maintenance_note: Slim trunk with a large knot and epicormic needle sprouts low on the stem; heavy lichen. Small for a 1999 planting (about 6.5 in DBH after 27 years), so growth is slow; check for root or soil problems.
notes: IMG_9372 shows this tree with a bigger larch beside it by the stone wall, plaque stake at its base.
